title: TRUNC
definition:
Returns a number truncated to a specified number of decimal places.
If decimal_places is provided, only that number of digits is kept after the decimal point (e.g. 21.35 → 21.3 with trunc(1)).
If no value is provided, the number is truncated to an integer (decimal part removed) without rounding.

title: ABS
definition:
Returns the absolute value of a number.
The result is always non-negative: negative values become positive, while positive values remain unchanged.

title: CEIL
definition:
Returns the smallest integer greater than or equal to the given number.
This means the value is always rounded up to the next integer if it has a decimal part.

title: FLOOR
definition:
Returns the largest integer less than or equal to the given number.
This means the value is always rounded down by removing the decimal part.

title: ROUND
definition:
Returns a number rounded to a specified number of decimal places.
If decimal_places is provided, the number is rounded to that precision (e.g. 21.35 → 21.4 with round(1)).
If no value is provided, the number is rounded to the nearest integer.

title: SQRT
definition:
Returns the square root of a numeric value.
The result is a number which, when multiplied by itself, equals the original value.

title: MOD
definition:
Returns the remainder of a division operation.
The function divides the column value by the given value and returns what is left after the division (e.g. 25 mod 10 = 5).

title: POWER
definition:
Raises a numeric value to a specified power.
The parameter n represents the exponent (e.g. pow(2) squares the value, pow(3) cubes it).
The result is calculated as x^n.

title: LOG
definition:
Returns the logarithm of a numeric value.
By default, the function computes the natural logarithm (base e).
If a base is provided, the logarithm is calculated using that base (e.g. log(2) = base 2).

title: EXP
definition:
Returns the exponential value of a numeric column.
The function computes e raised to the power of the column value (e^x).
This is the inverse operation of the logarithm function.
